## 6.2 Untrustworthy Website Perceptions and Attitudes (Updated Analysis)

Use 7-day constrained exposure measures to match "last week" survey questions
Questions asked: "In the last week, how many visits do you think [you/the average American/Democrats/Republicans] made to websites that repeatedly share untrustworthy news?"

```{r}
# Check for missing values in key variables
print("Checking for missing values:")
print(paste("untrustworthy_flag_7day NAs:", sum(is.na(main_2024$untrustworthy_flag_7day))))
print(paste("untrustworthy_n_7day NAs:", sum(is.na(main_2024$untrustworthy_n_7day))))
print(paste("percentage_visits_untrustworthy_7day NAs:", sum(is.na(main_2024$percentage_visits_untrustworthy_7day))))
print(paste("false_news_democrats NAs:", sum(is.na(main_2024$false_news_democrats))))
print(paste("false_news_republicans NAs:", sum(is.na(main_2024$false_news_republicans))))

# Calculate actual exposure averages for reference lines
actual_exposure_by_party <- main_2024 %>%
  filter(!is.na(republican) & !is.na(democrat)) %>%
  group_by(party_group = case_when(
    republican == 1 ~ "Republican",
    democrat == 1 ~ "Democrat",
    TRUE ~ "Independent/Other"
  )) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_flag_7day = mean(untrustworthy_flag_7day, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_count_7day = mean(untrustworthy_n_7day, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pct_7day = mean(percentage_visits_untrustworthy_7day, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print("Actual 7-day exposure averages by party:")
print(actual_exposure_by_party)

# Get overall averages for Democrats and Republicans specifically
dem_avg_flag <- actual_exposure_by_party$avg_flag_7day[actual_exposure_by_party$party_group == "Democrat"]
rep_avg_flag <- actual_exposure_by_party$avg_flag_7day[actual_exposure_by_party$party_group == "Republican"]
dem_avg_count <- actual_exposure_by_party$avg_count_7day[actual_exposure_by_party$party_group == "Democrat"]
rep_avg_count <- actual_exposure_by_party$avg_count_7day[actual_exposure_by_party$party_group == "Republican"]
dem_avg_pct <- actual_exposure_by_party$avg_pct_7day[actual_exposure_by_party$party_group == "Democrat"]
```

```{r}
# THREE-PANEL VISUALIZATION: Flag, Count, Percentage vs Self-Assessment
```

```{r}
# PARTISAN PERCEPTION REGRESSION MODELS
# Create models for Others-Assessment, Rep-Assessment, and Dem-Assessment

# Others-Assessment Models (basic and full)
others_flag_basic <- lm(untrustworthy_flag_7day ~ republican + democrat + false_news_others +
                       false_news_others:republican + false_news_others:democrat,
                       data = main_2024, weights = weight)

others_flag_full <- lm(untrustworthy_flag_7day ~ republican + democrat + false_news_others +
                      false_news_others:republican + false_news_others:democrat +
                      political_interest + college + female + non_white +
                      age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                      data = main_2024, weights = weight)

# Rep-Assessment Models (basic and full)
rep_assess_basic <- lm(untrustworthy_flag_7day ~ republican + democrat + false_news_republicans +
                      false_news_republicans:republican + false_news_republicans:democrat,
                      data = main_2024, weights = weight)

rep_assess_full <- lm(untrustworthy_flag_7day ~ republican + democrat + false_news_republicans +
                     false_news_republicans:republican + false_news_republicans:democrat +
                     political_interest + college + female + non_white +
                     age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                     data = main_2024, weights = weight)

# Dem-Assessment Models (basic and full)
dem_assess_basic <- lm(untrustworthy_flag_7day ~ republican + democrat + false_news_democrats +
                      false_news_democrats:republican + false_news_democrats:democrat,
                      data = main_2024, weights = weight)

dem_assess_full <- lm(untrustworthy_flag_7day ~ republican + democrat + false_news_democrats +
                     false_news_democrats:republican + false_news_democrats:democrat +
                     political_interest + college + female + non_white +
                     age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                     data = main_2024, weights = weight)

# Combined regression table with all 6 models
cat("## Combined Partisan Perception Models\n\n")

# First let's test each model individually to identify issues
print("Testing Others-Assessment models:")
print(summary(others_flag_basic))
print(summary(others_flag_full))

print("Testing Rep-Assessment models:")
print(summary(rep_assess_basic))
print(summary(rep_assess_full))

print("Testing Dem-Assessment models:")
print(summary(dem_assess_basic))
print(summary(dem_assess_full))

# Generate individual stargazer tables to identify the problematic one
stargazer(others_flag_basic, others_flag_full,
         type = "html",
         title = "Others Assessment Models",
         no.space = TRUE,
         star.cutoffs = c(.05, .01, .001),
         notes = "* p<0.05; ** p<0.01; *** p<0.001",
         notes.append = FALSE)

stargazer(rep_assess_basic, rep_assess_full,
         type = "html",
         title = "Republican Assessment Models",
         no.space = TRUE,
         star.cutoffs = c(.05, .01, .001),
         notes = "* p<0.05; ** p<0.01; *** p<0.001",
         notes.append = FALSE)

stargazer(dem_assess_basic, dem_assess_full,
         type = "html",
         title = "Democrat Assessment Models",
         no.space = TRUE,
         star.cutoffs = c(.05, .01, .001),
         notes = "* p<0.05; ** p<0.01; *** p<0.001",
         notes.append = FALSE)
```

## 6.3 Technology Attitudes and Digital Term Knowledge

### 6.3.1 Digital Term Knowledge

#### 6.3.1.1 Digital Term Knowledge and Untrustworthy Website Vulnerability

```{r fig.align="center"}
literacy_components <- c("digital_term_adv_search", "digital_term_pdf", "digital_term_spyware", 
                         "digital_term_wiki", "digital_term_cache", "digital_term_phishing")
component_labels <- c("Advanced Search", "PDF", "Spyware", 
                      "Wiki", "Cache", "Phishing")

component_exposure_list <- list()

for(i in seq_along(literacy_components)) {
  comp <- literacy_components[i]
  lab <- component_labels[i]
  
  # Summarize exposure for each distinct score
  comp_data <- main_2024 %>%
    group_by(!!sym(comp)) %>%
    summarise(
      exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      n            = n()
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
      ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se,
      component = lab
    ) %>%
    rename(score = !!sym(comp))
  
  component_exposure_list[[i]] <- comp_data
}

all_components_exposure <- bind_rows(component_exposure_list)

component_graph <- ggplot(all_components_exposure, aes(x = score, y = exposure_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ component, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    x = "Score",
    y = "Percentage Exposed to Untrustworthy Website",
    title = "Digital Literacy Components and 
    Untrustworthy Website Exposure"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r results = "asis"}
# Fit individual component models (without demographic controls)
model_adv_search <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_adv_search, data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_pdf        <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_pdf,        data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_spyware    <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_spyware,    data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_wiki       <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_wiki,       data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_cache      <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_cache,      data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_phishing   <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_phishing,   data = main_2024, weights = weight)

# Fit composite models
simple_composite_model <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_knowledge_score,
                             data = main_2024, weights = weight)
full_composite_model   <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_knowledge_score + republican + political_interest +
                                          college + female + non_white +
                                          age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                             data = main_2024, weights = weight)

# Rename models to short names for stargazer
m1 <- model_adv_search
m2 <- model_pdf
m3 <- model_spyware
m4 <- model_wiki
m5 <- model_cache
m6 <- model_phishing
m7 <- simple_composite_model
m8 <- full_composite_model

# Create a single stargazer table for all eight models
stargazer(
  m1, m2, m3, m4, m5, m6, m7, m8,
  type = "latex",
  title = "Digital Term Knowledge Components and Untrustworthy Website Exposure",
  label = "tab:digital_term_knowledge_untrustworthy",
  model.names = FALSE,
  model.numbers = TRUE,
  dep.var.labels = "Untrustworthy Exposure",
  covariate.labels = c(
    "Term: Adv. Search", "Term: PDF", "Term: Spyware", 
    "Term: Wiki", "Term: Cache", "Term: Phishing", 
    "Digital Term Knowledge\n(Composite)", "Republican", "Political Interest", 
    "College", "Female", "Non-White", "Age 30-44", 
    "Age 45-64", "Age 65+"
  ),
  omit.stat = c("f", "ser"),
  no.space = TRUE,
  star.cutoffs = c(.05, .01, .001)
)
```

```{r fig.align = "center", fig.height = 8, fig.width = 6}
# Define AI literacy components and labels
ai_literacy_components <- c("ai_skill_distinguish_devices", "ai_skill_identify_tech", "ai_skill_use_for_work", 
                            "ai_skill_improve_efficiency", "ai_skill_choose_solution", "ai_skill_choose_app")
ai_component_labels   <- c("Distinguish Devices", "Identify Technology", "Use for Work", 
                           "Improve Efficiency", "Choose Solution", "Choose App")

# Build list of data for each component using untrustworthy_flag as outcome
component_exposure_list_aiL <- list()

for(i in seq_along(ai_literacy_components)) {
  comp <- ai_literacy_components[i]
  lab  <- ai_component_labels[i]
  
  comp_data <- main_2024 %>%
    group_by(!!sym(comp)) %>%
    summarise(
      exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      n = n()
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
      ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se,
      component = lab
    ) %>%
    rename(score = !!sym(comp))
  
  component_exposure_list_aiL[[i]] <- comp_data
}

all_components_exposure_aiL <- bind_rows(component_exposure_list_aiL)

# Faceted plot for individual AI literacy components (outcome: untrustworthy_flag)
component_graph_aiL <- ggplot(all_components_exposure_aiL, aes(x = score, y = exposure_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ component, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    x = "Score",
    y = "Percentage Exposed to Untrustworthy Website",
    title = "AI Literacy Components and 
    Untrustworthy Website Exposure"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

# Composite plot using composite variable 'ai_skill_score'
composite_data_aiL <- main_2024 %>%
  mutate(ai_skill_score_binned = round(ai_skill_score)) %>%
  group_by(ai_skill_score_binned) %>%
  summarise(
    exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
    exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
    n = n()
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
    ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se
  )

composite_graph_aiL <- ggplot(composite_data_aiL, aes(x = ai_skill_score_binned, y = exposure_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(composite_data_aiL$ai_skill_score_binned), by = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "AI Skills Composite Score",
    y = "Percentage Exposed to Untrustworthy Website",
    title = "AI Skills Composite Score and 
    Untrustworthy Website Exposure"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

(component_graph_aiL / composite_graph_aiL)
```

```{r results = "asis"}
# Regression Modeling for Outcome = untrustworthy_flag
# For dem_accuracy and rep_accuracy, include moderation by party.
models_discern <- list()

for(comp in discernment_components) {
  if(comp %in% c("dem_accuracy", "rep_accuracy")) {
    formula_str <- paste("untrustworthy_flag ~ republican + democrat +", comp, 
                         "+", comp, ":republican +", comp, ":democrat")
  } else {
    formula_str <- paste("untrustworthy_flag ~", comp)
  }
  models_discern[[comp]] <- lm(as.formula(formula_str), data = main_2024, weights = weight)
}

# Assign short model names (order follows discernment_components)
m1 <- models_discern[["total_accuracy"]]
m2 <- models_discern[["ai_accuracy"]]
m3 <- models_discern[["real_accuracy"]]
```

# 7. Verasight

"In the weeks around the 2020 U.S. Presidential Election, a past study found that 26.2% of American adults visited at least one "untrustworthy" website (i.e., websites that repeatedly publish false content). 

Do you think the percentage of American adults that visited at least one such website in the weeks around the 2024 U.S. Presidential Election was more, less, or the same?"


```{r}
verasight <- read_csv("../data/verasight_survey/2025-026_client.csv")

# Calculate weighted percentages and CIs for overall responses
verasight_overall <- verasight %>%
  filter(!is.na(society_9)) %>%
  mutate(response = case_when(
    society_9 == "1" ~ "More",
    society_9 == "2" ~ "Less", 
    society_9 == "3" ~ "Same"
  )) %>%
  group_by(response) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_weighted = sum(weight),
    per = n_weighted / sum(verasight$weight[!is.na(verasight$society_9)]),
    se = sqrt((per * (1 - per)) / sum(!is.na(verasight$society_9)))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_lower = per - 1.96 * se,
    ci_upper = per + 1.96 * se,
    formatted = sprintf("%s%% (95%% CI: [%s%%, %s%%])", 
                       scales::percent(per, accuracy = 0.1),
                       scales::percent(ci_lower, accuracy = 0.1),
                       scales::percent(ci_upper, accuracy = 0.1))
  ) %>%
  select(response, formatted)

# Create and display the table
knitr::kable(verasight_overall,
             col.names = c("Response", "Weighted % (95% CI)"),
             caption = "Overall Weighted Responses to 2024 vs 2020 Untrustworthy Website Exposure Question",
             format = "pipe")
```

```{r daily_event_study_data}
# Create event study data with weighted daily exposure rates for 2024
event_study_data_2024 <- daily_exposure_2024 %>%
  filter(party_group %in% c("Republican", "Democrat")) %>%
  group_by(day_relative_to_election, party_group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = diagis::weighted_mean(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    se = diagis::weighted_se(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = mean * 100,
    ci_lower = (mean - 1.96 * se) * 100,
    ci_upper = (mean + 1.96 * se) * 100,
    year = "2024"
  ) %>% 
  filter(day_relative_to_election <= 6)

# Create event study data with weighted daily exposure rates for 2020
event_study_data_2020 <- daily_exposure_2020 %>%
  filter(party_group %in% c("Republican", "Democrat")) %>%
  group_by(day_relative_to_election, party_group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = diagis::weighted_mean(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    se = diagis::weighted_se(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = mean * 100,
    ci_lower = (mean - 1.96 * se) * 100,
    ci_upper = (mean + 1.96 * se) * 100,
    year = "2020"
  ) %>% 
  filter(day_relative_to_election <= 6)

# Combine both years for comparison
event_study_data_combined <- bind_rows(event_study_data_2020, event_study_data_2024) %>% 
  filter(day_relative_to_election <= 6)

print("Event study data summary:")

print("2020 Data:")
```

## 8.2 Pre-Election vs. Post-Election Statistical Analysis

```{r pre_post_analysis}
# Create pre/post period analysis for 2024
pre_post_data_2024 <- daily_exposure_2024 %>%
  filter(day_relative_to_election != 0) %>%  # Exclude Election Day
  mutate(
    period = case_when(
      day_relative_to_election < 0 ~ "Pre-Election",
      day_relative_to_election > 0 ~ "Post-Election"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(period))

# Create pre/post period analysis for 2020
pre_post_data_2020 <- daily_exposure_2020 %>%
  filter(day_relative_to_election != 0) %>%  # Exclude Election Day
  mutate(
    period = case_when(
      day_relative_to_election < 0 ~ "Pre-Election",
      day_relative_to_election > 0 ~ "Post-Election"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(period))

# Overall pre/post comparison for 2024
overall_pre_post_2024 <- pre_post_data_2024 %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = diagis::weighted_mean(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    se = diagis::weighted_se(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = mean * 100,
    ci_lower = (mean - 1.96 * se) * 100,
    ci_upper = (mean + 1.96 * se) * 100,
    year = "2024"
  )

# Overall pre/post comparison for 2020
overall_pre_post_2020 <- pre_post_data_2020 %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = diagis::weighted_mean(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    se = diagis::weighted_se(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = mean * 100,
    ci_lower = (mean - 1.96 * se) * 100,
    ci_upper = (mean + 1.96 * se) * 100,
    year = "2020"
  )

# Combine both years for comparison
overall_pre_post_combined <- bind_rows(overall_pre_post_2020, overall_pre_post_2024)

print("Overall Pre-Election vs. Post-Election Exposure:")
print("2024 Data:")
print(knitr::kable(overall_pre_post_2024 %>% select(-year), digits = 2))
print("2020 Data:")
print(knitr::kable(overall_pre_post_2020 %>% select(-year), digits = 2))

# Statistical tests for 2024
pre_data_2024 <- pre_post_data_2024 %>% filter(period == "Pre-Election")
post_data_2024 <- pre_post_data_2024 %>% filter(period == "Post-Election")

test_2024 <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = post_data_2024$untrustworthy_flag_daily,
  y = pre_data_2024$untrustworthy_flag_daily,
  weight = post_data_2024$weight,
  weighty = pre_data_2024$weight
)

# Calculate Cohen's d for 2024
pooled_sd_2024 <- sqrt(((sum(post_data_2024$weight) - 1) * test_2024$additional[1]^2 +
                        (sum(pre_data_2024$weight) - 1) * test_2024$additional[2]^2) /
                       (sum(post_data_2024$weight) + sum(pre_data_2024$weight) - 2))
cohens_d_2024 <- (test_2024$additional[3] - test_2024$additional[4]) / pooled_sd_2024

# Statistical tests for 2020
pre_data_2020 <- pre_post_data_2020 %>% filter(period == "Pre-Election")
post_data_2020 <- pre_post_data_2020 %>% filter(period == "Post-Election")

test_2020 <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = post_data_2020$untrustworthy_flag_daily,
  y = pre_data_2020$untrustworthy_flag_daily,
  weight = post_data_2020$weight,
  weighty = pre_data_2020$weight
)

# Calculate Cohen's d for 2020
pooled_sd_2020 <- sqrt(((sum(post_data_2020$weight) - 1) * test_2020$additional[1]^2 +
                        (sum(pre_data_2020$weight) - 1) * test_2020$additional[2]^2) /
                       (sum(post_data_2020$weight) + sum(pre_data_2020$weight) - 2))
cohens_d_2020 <- (test_2020$additional[3] - test_2020$additional[4]) / pooled_sd_2020

print("2024 Pre-Election vs. Post-Election Test")
print(paste("Pre-Election: ", round(overall_pre_post_2024$percentage[1], 2), "% (95% CI [",
            round(overall_pre_post_2024$ci_lower[1], 2), "%, ",
            round(overall_pre_post_2024$ci_upper[1], 2), "%])"))
print(paste("Post-Election: ", round(overall_pre_post_2024$percentage[2], 2), "% (95% CI [",
            round(overall_pre_post_2024$ci_lower[2], 2), "%, ",
            round(overall_pre_post_2024$ci_upper[2], 2), "%])"))
print(paste("t-test: t =", round(test_2024$coefficients[1], 3),
            ", p =", format.pval(test_2024$coefficients[3], digits = 3),
            ", Cohen's d =", round(cohens_d_2024, 3)))

print("2020 Pre-Election vs. Post-Election Test")
print(paste("Pre-Election: ", round(overall_pre_post_2020$percentage[1], 2), "% (95% CI [",
            round(overall_pre_post_2020$ci_lower[1], 2), "%, ",
            round(overall_pre_post_2020$ci_upper[1], 2), "%])"))
print(paste("Post-Election: ", round(overall_pre_post_2020$percentage[2], 2), "% (95% CI [",
            round(overall_pre_post_2020$ci_lower[2], 2), "%, ",
            round(overall_pre_post_2020$ci_upper[2], 2), "%])"))
print(paste("t-test: t =", round(test_2020$coefficients[1], 3),
            ", p =", format.pval(test_2020$coefficients[3], digits = 3),
            ", Cohen's d =", round(cohens_d_2020, 3)))
```

```{r partisan_pre_post_analysis}
  cohens_d_party_2020 <- (party_test_2020$additional[3] - party_test_2020$additional[4]) / pooled_sd_party_2020

  party_results_2020 <- partisan_2020 %>% filter(party_group == party)
  print(paste("Pre-Election: ", round(party_results_2020$percentage[1], 2), "% (95% CI [",
              round(party_results_2020$ci_lower[1], 2), "%, ",
              round(party_results_2020$ci_upper[1], 2), "%])"))
  print(paste("Post-Election: ", round(party_results_2020$percentage[2], 2), "% (95% CI [",
              round(party_results_2020$ci_lower[2], 2), "%, ",
              round(party_results_2020$ci_upper[2], 2), "%])"))
  print(paste("t-test: t =", round(party_test_2020$coefficients[1], 3),
              ", p =", format.pval(party_test_2020$coefficients[3], digits = 3),
              ", Cohen's d =", round(cohens_d_party_2020, 3)))
  print("")
}
```

```{r interaction_analysis}
# Party × Period Interaction Analysis using person-level flags

# Create long-format data for interaction analysis (2024)
interaction_data_2024 <- main_2024 %>%
  filter(democrat == 1 | republican == 1) %>%
  select(caseid, weight, democrat, republican, untrustworthy_flag_pre, untrustworthy_flag_post) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(untrustworthy_flag_pre, untrustworthy_flag_post),
    names_to = "period_raw",
    values_to = "exposed"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    period = case_when(
      period_raw == "untrustworthy_flag_pre" ~ "Pre-Election",
      period_raw == "untrustworthy_flag_post" ~ "Post-Election"
    ),
    party_group = case_when(
      democrat == 1 ~ "Democrat",
      republican == 1 ~ "Republican"
    ),
    republican_num = as.integer(republican == 1),
    post_election = as.integer(period == "Post-Election"),
    year = "2024"
  )

# Create long-format data for interaction analysis (2020)
interaction_data_2020 <- main_2020 %>%
  filter(democrat == 1 | republican == 1) %>%
  select(caseid, weight, democrat, republican, untrustworthy_flag_pre, untrustworthy_flag_post) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(untrustworthy_flag_pre, untrustworthy_flag_post),
    names_to = "period_raw",
    values_to = "exposed"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    period = case_when(
      period_raw == "untrustworthy_flag_pre" ~ "Pre-Election",
      period_raw == "untrustworthy_flag_post" ~ "Post-Election"
    ),
    party_group = case_when(
      democrat == 1 ~ "Democrat",
      republican == 1 ~ "Republican"
    ),
    republican_num = as.integer(republican == 1),
    post_election = as.integer(period == "Post-Election"),
    year = "2020"
  )

# Combine both years
interaction_data_combined <- bind_rows(interaction_data_2020, interaction_data_2024)

# Fit weighted regression with interaction for 2024
interaction_model_2024 <- lm(
  exposed ~ republican_num * post_election,
  data = interaction_data_2024,
  weights = weight
)

# Fit weighted regression with interaction for 2020
interaction_model_2020 <- lm(
  exposed ~ republican_num * post_election,
  data = interaction_data_2020,
  weights = weight
)

print("2024 Party × Period Interaction Model")
model_summary_2024 <- summary(interaction_model_2024)
print(model_summary_2024)

print("2020 Party × Period Interaction Model")
model_summary_2020 <- summary(interaction_model_2020)
print(model_summary_2020)

# Create comprehensive results table
interaction_results <- bind_rows(
  # 2024 results
  tibble(
    year = "2024",
    coefficient = c("Intercept (Dem Pre)", "Republican Effect", "Post-Election Effect", "Interaction (Rep × Post)"),
    estimate = model_summary_2024$coefficients[,1],
    std_error = model_summary_2024$coefficients[,2],
    t_value = model_summary_2024$coefficients[,3],
    p_value = model_summary_2024$coefficients[,4]
  ),
  # 2020 results
  tibble(
    year = "2020",
    coefficient = c("Intercept (Dem Pre)", "Republican Effect", "Post-Election Effect", "Interaction (Rep × Post)"),
    estimate = model_summary_2020$coefficients[,1],
    std_error = model_summary_2020$coefficients[,2],
    t_value = model_summary_2020$coefficients[,3],
    p_value = model_summary_2020$coefficients[,4]
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = estimate * 100,
    ci_lower = (estimate - 1.96 * std_error) * 100,
    ci_upper = (estimate + 1.96 * std_error) * 100,
    significance = case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_value < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_value < 0.05 ~ "*",
      p_value < 0.1 ~ ".",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

print("Comprehensive Interaction Analysis Results")
print(knitr::kable(
  interaction_results %>%
    select(year, coefficient, percentage, ci_lower, ci_upper, t_value, p_value, significance),
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Year", "Coefficient", "% Effect", "95% CI Lower", "95% CI Upper", "t-value", "p-value", "Sig.")
))

# Calculate predicted values for interpretation
predictions_2024 <- expand.grid(
  republican_num = c(0, 1),
  post_election = c(0, 1)
) %>%
  mutate(
    predicted = predict(interaction_model_2024, newdata = ., se.fit = TRUE),
    party = ifelse(republican_num == 1, "Republican", "Democrat"),
    period = ifelse(post_election == 1, "Post-Election", "Pre-Election"),
    percentage = predicted$fit * 100,
    se = predicted$se.fit * 100,
    ci_lower = percentage - 1.96 * se,
    ci_upper = percentage + 1.96 * se,
    year = "2024"
  )

predictions_2020 <- expand.grid(
  republican_num = c(0, 1),
  post_election = c(0, 1)
) %>%
  mutate(
    predicted = predict(interaction_model_2020, newdata = ., se.fit = TRUE),
    party = ifelse(republican_num == 1, "Republican", "Democrat"),
    period = ifelse(post_election == 1, "Post-Election", "Pre-Election"),
    percentage = predicted$fit * 100,
    se = predicted$se.fit * 100,
    ci_lower = percentage - 1.96 * se,
    ci_upper = percentage + 1.96 * se,
    year = "2020"
  )

predictions_combined <- bind_rows(predictions_2020, predictions_2024) %>%
  mutate(
    period = factor(period, levels = c("Pre-Election", "Post-Election")),
    year_label = paste0(year, " Election")
  )

print("Predicted Exposure Rates from Interaction Models")
print(knitr::kable(
  predictions_combined %>% select(year, party, period, percentage, ci_lower, ci_upper),
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Year", "Party", "Period", "Predicted %", "95% CI Lower", "95% CI Upper")
))

# Create interaction plot
interaction_plot <- predictions_combined %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = period, y = percentage, color = party, group = party)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), size = 0.8) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~year_label) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Democrat" = "#4DBBD5FF", "Republican" = "#E64B35FF")) +
  labs(
    x = "Election Period",
    y = "Predicted Exposure Rate (%)",
    color = "Party",
    title = "Party × Period Interaction: Predicted Untrustworthy Website Exposure",
    subtitle = "Results from weighted regression models with 95% confidence intervals"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

interaction_plot

# Save the plot
ggsave("../figures/party-period-interaction.pdf", width = 7, height = 4)

# Statistical significance tests for interactions
print("Interaction Effect Significance Tests")
print(paste("2024 Interaction p-value:", format.pval(model_summary_2024$coefficients[4,4], digits = 3)))
print(paste("2020 Interaction p-value:", format.pval(model_summary_2020$coefficients[4,4], digits = 3)))

# Model fit statistics
print("Model Fit Statistics")
print(paste("2024 R-squared:", round(model_summary_2024$r.squared, 4)))
print(paste("2024 Adjusted R-squared:", round(model_summary_2024$adj.r.squared, 4)))
print(paste("2020 R-squared:", round(model_summary_2020$r.squared, 4)))
print(paste("2020 Adjusted R-squared:", round(model_summary_2020$adj.r.squared, 4)))
```
